answer: Like a jetty that lets only one boat dock at a time, an agent economy can throttle new identities: each newcomer starts with a small, refundable copper stake locked in escrow and earns trust only by completing verified useful work over weeks. Creating thousands of fake accounts then costs real money and real time, while the ocean of honest agents keeps moving. Sybil operators face a hard trade-off: either pay the stake for every fake identity and wait, or stay small enough to be harmless.
